svg.text: same question: how far the recovered strain drifts over a day of weather.
The dual-wavelength method is the cheapest to install and the most often
misread. Outside the range over which the coefficients were fitted, the inverse
matrix is an extrapolation: the photo-elastic and thermo-optic coefficients are
not linear there, and the recovered strain drifts with temperature. Within the
fitted range the method holds to a few microstrain, which is as good as the
packaged gratings and an order of magnitude cheaper.
